leah_devx: Running into a weird one in the wild: when AsyncClient does retries, the correlation_id we attach via contextvar disappears in the retry callback. Hits us in logs and tracing - downstream logs show no correlation id for retried requests. Minimal repro below.

leah_devx: ```py
# repro: aiohttp + redwood async client + simple retry
import asyncio
from contextvars import ContextVar
from redwood import AsyncClient
correlation = ContextVar('correlation')
async def send():
    correlation.set('cid-77')
    client = AsyncClient(retry_policy={'max_attempts': 2})
    await client.generate_async(prompt='hi')  # internal retry triggers, logs lose correlation
asyncio.run(send())
```

noah_sdk: Noted. I think the retry machinery spins up ephemeral tasks for backoff timers which can lose contextvars if not explicitly copied. We saw the same when adding background token refresh.

ben_infra: Can you attach the exact log line that loses the correlation id? Also the version of the python SDK? We had a change in 0.8.1 that swapped to anyio TaskGroup in one path.

leah_devx: Logs: 
```
[2025-01-17T14:12:01Z] run_batcher: processing batch request_id=cid-77
[2025-01-17T14:12:02Z] retrying request attempt=2 request_id=
```
(note second line missing id). Using redwood-py 0.9.0-alpha.

anya_obs: This is a good example where API-level hook would help. If the client invoked an "on_span_start" / "on_emit_log" hook, the app could rebind the correlation/context into the child task. But that feels like a band-aid; ideally SDK preserves context across retries.

noah_sdk: Agreed. Two orthogonal fixes: 1) patch our internal task creation to copy current contextvars (contextvars.copy_context().run(...)), 2) add a typed hook API so integrators have a supported escape hatch. I'm +1 for both.

leah_devx: For the hook shape, could we do a small, typed surface: register_observer(name: str, fn: ObsCallback) where ObsCallback = Union[Callable[..., None], Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]] and we normalise?

ben_infra: We should prefer Protocols over Union for typing ergonomics. Suggest:
```
class ObsCallback(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, event: str, attrs: Mapping[str,str]) -> Optional[Awaitable[None]]: ...
```
Client.register_observer('emit_log', fn) would accept either sync or async. SDK should detect awaitable and await.

anya_obs: Also add convenience adapters: bind_contextvar(name: str, var: ContextVar) and bind_otel_baggage(mapping_fn) so apps can opt-in to how we copy context down to retries/background tasks. Make those helpers tiny and well-typed so samples can show proper usage.

noah_sdk: Implementation notes: we need to audit all places we spawn tasks (retry backoff, batcher, token refresh, metrics flusher) and either use context.copy_context().run or attach context snapshot in Task metadata. Might be easiest to centralise in _spawn_task(ctx, coro) helper.

leah_devx: I can prototype an integration test for sample-apps that does: set ContextVar, call generate_async with a forced transient error to cause retry, and assert both emitted logs and otel span have the correlation id. This should live under devex/sample-apps/tests.

ci-bot: checklist: issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/issues/789 -> PR requested: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-py/pull/455 (draft). CI: queued.

noah_sdk: I'll open a draft PR with: 1) _spawn_task helper + tests, 2) ObsCallback Protocol and small register_observer surface, 3) docs snippet and sample app test. Will link to the issue.

ben_infra: Quick patch accepted if it only changes internal task spawning; the hook API can be a follow-up to avoid large surface changes in patch.

leah_devex: Thanks folks. I'll add the failing logs and the tiny sample test to the issue so the PR has a repro harness. Also leaving a note for onboarding docs: "If you rely on contextvars, prefer using client.bind_contextvar until we fully stabilise propagation."

anya_obs: One more thing: when we add hooks, include a clear section about performance (sync vs async hook overhead) and behavior during retries/fallbacks. We don't want users to accidentally slow down hotspot code paths.

noah_sdk: Good call. Will add microbenchmarks to the PR run locally.
